summary: Autonomous Chaos Engineering audit completed across 3 microservice targets. The architecture demonstrated an overall resilience score of 74/100. The automated safety watchdog successfully guarded all tests, preventing catastrophic system crashes. Key vulnerabilities identified in synchronous cart dependency and catalog response throttling.

vulnerabilities.title: Cascading Outage on Cart Dependency Outage
vulnerabilities.description: Frontend lacks local session storage or circuit-breaking for cart operations. Unavailability of cart container halts user shopping workflow and propagates 5xx errors.
vulnerabilities.impact: Severe direct checkout and revenue loss; storefront degraded.

vulnerabilities.title: Product Catalog Latency Propagation Under Resource Exhaustion
vulnerabilities.description: CPU starvation causes catalog p95 latency to peak at 7.1ms. Synchronous calls from frontend block worker threads waiting on catalog responses.
vulnerabilities.impact: Homepage rendering time spikes, driving user drop-off.

vulnerabilities.title: Non-Critical Service Degradation Blast Radius
vulnerabilities.description: Service recommendation disruption induced MTTR of 0.10s before telemetry stabilized back to baseline.
vulnerabilities.impact: Subsystem delay without immediate catastrophic outage.

prescribed_fixes.recommendation: Implement an Envoy/gRPC circuit breaker between frontend and cart. Fallback to client-side localStorage or read-only cart view with asynchronous queueing for pending add-to-cart events.
Deploy an in-memory Redis/Valkey cache layer for high-demand product IDs with a 60-second TTL. Enforce strict client-side timeouts (max 400ms) with stale-while-revalidate fallback.
Wrap recommendation calls in non-blocking async promises with empty fallbacks and exponential backoff retry policies.
